steps.text: I'm a developer. Like a lot of developers, I now hand work to coding agents that run in the cloud for hours.
Here's the problem. To check on them, or give them direction, I need to be at a screen. When I step away, the agent either waits for me, or it guesses.
And voice mode doesn't fix it. It just reads the text aloud.

Here's a summary. Hash, test results. Two hundred twelve passed, two failed. Failed tests. Bullet. Test underscore checkout underscore currency, line forty-two, assertion error, expected nineteen point nine nine, got nineteen point nine eight.
What I need is a real voice. One that listens, summarises, asks before it acts, and calls me back when the work is done.
{{product}} gives every text agent a real voice, and a phone number.
Here's my coding agent. It runs in the cloud, and now it has a phone number. I'm out for a walk, so I call it.
Hey. Did last night's test run pass?
Mostly. Two hundred twelve of two hundred fourteen tests passed. Two checkout tests failed after yesterday's payment change. Want me to look into it?
Yes. Fix them and open a pull request. But don't merge.
Got it. I'll fix both tests and open a pull request, without merging. It'll take a few minutes. I'll call you back.
I hang up. The agent keeps working in the cloud.
Hi, it's your coding agent. I found it: a rounding bug in the new currency code. Both tests pass now. One question first. Refunds use the same code. Should I fix them too?
Done. All two hundred fourteen tests pass, and the pull request is open. I've texted you the link.
The agent did the work. {{product}} did the talking. It summarised, it asked before deciding, and it called me back.
Any agent that runs in the cloud can have a real voice, and a phone number.
